newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRANCE EXPECTS SECOND LARGEST MAIZE CROP.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE EXPECTS SECOND LARGEST MAIZE CROP.

text.p: The French farm ministry on Tuesday predicted a 1997 maize harvest of 14.934 million tonnes, up 2.8 percent from 1996 and the country's second biggest maize crop.

It also projected a second-largest soft wheat crop of 33.217 million tonnes -- unchanged from a previous report -- but a 25.3 percent slide in the production of drought-hit durum wheat to 937,000 tonnes.
This is a cut from last month's forecast of 974,000 tonnes.
The ministry's latest estimates, including the first for maize, were published by the SCEES statistics office and confirm outlines given by French grain sources on Monday.
The ministry saw 10 million tonnes of barley production, revised up from 9.683 million tonnes published in July and 5.3 percent ahead of last year's harvest of 9.497 million tonnes.
For oilseeds, the ministry forecast a record rapeseed crop of 3.15 million tonnes, revised up from 2.847 million tones last month and 8.2 percent higher than last year.
In its first forecast for late-harvested sunflower, it gave output of 2.19 million tonnes, up 9.7 percent on last year.
It forecast total oilseed production at 5.61 million tonnes, up 9.2 percent from 1996.
